Robust trend smoothing with post-smoothing bands and re-smoothing

Source: R/smoothers.R
robust_smooth.Rd

Extracts a trend from each weekly series (one per key) with one of eight smoothers, places a band around the fitted values (trend + seasonal), flags the observed weeks outside the band, sets them to missing and smooths again. No cleaning is applied before the first smoothing.

Usage

robust_smooth(
  dt,
  key_cols,
  time_col,
  value_col,
  method = c("henderson", "loess", "gam_ar1", "whittaker", "level", "llt", "smooth",
    "smooth_t"),
  transform = c("log1p", "log", "none"),
  period = 365.25/7,
  harmonics = NULL,
  max_harmonics = 6L,
  n_backfit = 3L,
  band = c("model", "mad"),
  z = 3.5,
  k = 3.5,
  max_iter = 2L,
  run_min = 4L,
  nu = 4,
  level = 0.95,
  flag_na = c("all", "isolated"),
  q_select = c("gaussian", "profile_t"),
  log10_q_grid = seq(-6, 1, by = 0.25),
  damping = c("none", "profile"),
  phi_grid = c(seq(0.8, 0.98, by = 0.02), 0.99, 1)
)

Arguments

dt

A data.frame or data.table with one row per key x week.

key_cols

Character vector of key columns identifying each series.

time_col

Name of the time column (class Date or IDate, weekly).

value_col

Name of the value column (counts for log1p, positive for log); NA allowed.

method

Smoother: "henderson", "loess", "gam_ar1", "whittaker", "level", "llt", "smooth" or "smooth_t".

transform

Scale of the model: "log1p" (default), "log" or "none".

period

Seasonal period in weeks (default 365.25 / 7).

harmonics

Fixed number of Fourier harmonics, or NULL to choose it by AICc of the smooth model.

max_harmonics

Largest number of harmonics considered when harmonics = NULL.

n_backfit

Number of backfitting iterations.

band

"model" (auxiliary-residual band for Kalman methods, MAD band otherwise) or "mad" (MAD band for every method).

z

Half-width multiplier of the model band (in standard deviations).

k

Half-width multiplier of the MAD band (in robust standard deviations, 1.4826 * MAD).

max_iter

Maximum number of re-smoothings after pass 1 (non-negative integer; 0 = pass 1 only).

run_min

Minimum length in weeks of a run of flags that is not isolated.

nu

Degrees of freedom of the Student-t weights (smooth_t).

level

Confidence level of trend_lo, trend_hi.

flag_na

"all" (every flagged week is set to missing in the next pass) or "isolated" (only the weeks of isolated runs).

q_select

Choice of q for smooth_t: "gaussian" (default; the ML value of the Gaussian smooth trend model) or "profile_t" (maximum of the profile objective under the Student-t model, see Details). Other methods accept only the default.

log10_q_grid

Grid of \(\log_{10} q\) values searched when q_select = "profile_t".

damping

"none" (default, \(\phi = 1\)) or "profile" (damped slope, \(\phi\) profiled jointly with q on phi_grid; requires q_select = "profile_t", method smooth_t only).

phi_grid

Grid of damping factors in (0, 1] searched when damping = "profile".

Value

A data.table ordered by key and time with columns key_cols, time_col (IDate), observed (transformed scale, NA for missing weeks), seasonal, trend, trend_se (NA for henderson, loess, whittaker), trend_lo, trend_hi, remainder (observed - seasonal - trend), trend_pass1, band_lo, band_hi, excluded, flag_1, flag_2 (NA when pass 2 was not run), flag, flag_type (NA for unflagged weeks), pass (final pass of the key), method, weight (final Student-t weight, smooth_t only) and flag_weight (weight < (nu + 1) / (nu + z^2)). Attributes: fits (one row per key x pass with pass, K, aicc_K, parameter, value, criterion, criterion_value, edf, rho, ic_ratio, var_level, var_slope, var_obs, band, band_defined, n_excluded, n_flag, iterations (IRLS, smooth_t), irls_converged, q_select, phi, loglik_profile, q_at_edge, phi_at_edge (smooth_t, see Details), final, converged, error), flags (one row per run of flag with start, end, n_weeks, flag_type, shift, half_width), transform, observed_transform, key_cols, time_col, period, method and band.

Details

Scale. The series is modelled on the scale of transform. log1p keeps zero weeks; in the output attributes it is recorded as transform = "log" (and observed_transform = "log1p"), so that trend_index() with transform = "log" and trend_diagnostics() treat the log1p trend as a log trend: the index is exp of differences of log(1 + n), close to differences of log(n) when counts are large.

Seasonality. The seasonal component is a Fourier regression with period period and t the number of weeks since 1970-01-01 (as in extract_trend()). The number of harmonics K is chosen once per key and pass by the AICc of the smooth Kalman model (extract_trend() with method = "smooth", on the series with the excluded weeks set to NA), or fixed by harmonics, and is shared by every method, so that methods differ only in the trend filter. The seasonal coefficients are estimated by backfitting (n_backfit iterations, as in extract_trend()) with the trend filter of the method, except gam_ar1, which has the harmonics in its formula.

Methods (each smoothing parameter is chosen from the data):

  • henderson: henderson_filter() with the length chosen by GCV among 13, 23 and 39 (lengths longer than the series are skipped) and the Musgrave end weights with the I/C ratio of a preliminary 13-term pass. Missing weeks of the input are linearly interpolated; excluded weeks are replaced by the fitted values (trend + seasonal) of the previous pass (X-11 style).

  • loess: stats::loess(degree = 1, family = "symmetric") on time, with the span chosen on the grid 0.06, 0.08, ..., 0.50 by the GCV of the gaussian fit, n RSS / (n - trace.hat)^2; surface = "direct" so that the trend extends to missing weeks at the ends.

  • gam_ar1: mgcv::bam(y ~ s(t, bs = "cr", k = 40) + Fourier, rho, AR.start, method = "fREML") (k reduced on short series), with rho on the grid 0, 0.05, ..., 0.9 chosen at the minimum fREML score; AR.start marks the first week after each missing stretch. The trend is the intercept plus the spline, trend_se its standard error from the Bayesian covariance matrix. Requires mgcv.

  • whittaker: whittaker_smooth() of order 2 with \(\lambda\) by GCV; missing weeks get weight zero.

  • level: Kalman local level, stats::StructTS(type = "level") and stats::KalmanSmooth(), by maximum likelihood.

  • llt, smooth: the local linear trend and the smooth trend model (level variance 0) of extract_trend(), by maximum likelihood.

  • smooth_t: robust Kalman smoother. It starts from the smooth ML fit (seasonal component, observation variance \(\hat h\), signal-to-noise ratio q = var_slope / var_obs), then iterates (at most 20 times) a Kalman filter and Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother of the same model with time-varying observation variance \(h_t = \hat h / w_t\), with Student-t weights \(w_t = (\nu + 1) / (\nu + s_t^2)\), \(s_t^2 = (e_t^2 + P_{t|n}) / \hat h\) (EM weights; \(e_t\) the auxiliary residual, \(P_{t|n}\) the smoothed level variance), and \(\hat h\) re-estimated as the weighted mean of \(e_t^2 + P_{t|n}\). With q_select = "gaussian" (default) q is kept fixed, so the smoothness of the ML fit is kept and only the weights change. The seasonal coefficients are re-estimated by weighted least squares in the backfitting. The final weights are returned in weight.

smooth_t: q under the t model and damped slope. With q_select = "profile_t", q is chosen on the grid \(10^g\), g in log10_q_grid, by maximising $$L(q, \phi) = \ell_G(q, \phi; h_t = \hat h / w_t) + \sum_t \log \mathrm{Gamma}(w_t; \nu/2, \nu/2),$$ where, for each grid point, the IRLS is run to convergence from \(w_t = 1\) and the \(\hat h\) of the Gaussian fit, \(\ell_G\) is the Gaussian log-likelihood of the seasonally adjusted series by prediction-error decomposition under observation variance \(h_t\) and slope variance \(q \hat h\), with the first two prediction errors (the diffuse elements of the initial state) left out for every grid point, and the sum runs over the observed weeks (Gamma density with shape and rate \(\nu/2\)). To keep one IRLS per grid point, the seasonal component is estimated once by the backfitting at the Gaussian q and held fixed during the grid search; the full backfitting is then run at the selected point. With damping = "profile" (requires q_select = "profile_t") the slope is damped, \(\beta_{t+1} = \phi \beta_t + \eta_t\), \(\eta_t \sim N(0, q \hat h)\), level variance 0, with both states diffuse at the start for every \(\phi\), and \((q, \phi)\) is profiled jointly on log10_q_grid x phi_grid. fits reports q_select, the selected q (value), phi, loglik_profile (the objective at the selected point, with the seasonal of the grid search), q_at_edge (selected q at the minimum or maximum of the grid), phi_at_edge (selected \(\phi < 1\) at the minimum of phi_grid; \(\phi = 1\) is not an edge), and the IRLS iterations and irls_converged of the final fit. The grid search multiplies the cost of a smooth_t pass by about the number of grid points.

Bands. With band = "model", the Kalman methods (level, llt, smooth, smooth_t) use the auxiliary-residual band trend + seasonal +/- z * sqrt(v_t). For an observed week used in the fit, \(v_t = \hat h - P_{t|n}\) (variance of the auxiliary residual, \(P_{t|n}\) the smoothed trend variance). In general \(v_t = (1 - k_t)^2 \hat h + (1 - k_t) P_{t|n}\) with \(k_t = P_{t|n} / h_t\) the weight of the week in its own smoothed trend: it equals \(\hat h - P_{t|n}\) when \(h_t = \hat h\), and \(\hat h + P_{t|n}\) (prediction variance) for weeks excluded from the fit (\(k_t = 0\)). For smooth_t, \(h_t = \hat h / w_t\): a down-weighted week is judged against the scale \(\hat h\), not against its inflated \(h_t\). The seasonal coefficients are treated as known. Negative values of \(v_t\) from rounding are set to 0. When \(\hat h\) is not finite or not above 1e-8 times the variance of the series of the pass (the ML fit interpolates the data, as happens for level and llt when the observation variance is estimated at 0), the band is undefined: band_lo, band_hi and the flags of the key are NA, no further pass is run, band_defined is FALSE in fits, converged is NA, and a single warning lists the keys concerned. Non-Kalman methods with band = "model", and every method with band = "mad", use trend + seasonal +/- k * 1.4826 * MAD(remainder), the MAD computed on the weeks used in the fit of that pass.

Weights. For smooth_t, weight holds the final Student-t weight \(w_t\) of the weeks used in the final fit and flag_weight is \(w_t < (\nu + 1) / (\nu + z^2)\), i.e. \(s_t > z\): the week is down-weighted as much as a standardised residual beyond the band multiplier z. Both are NA for other methods and for weeks not used in the final fit.

Passes. Pass 1 smooths the series as observed and flags the observed weeks outside the band (flag_1). Pass 2 sets the flagged weeks to NA (with flag_na = "isolated", only the weeks of isolated runs) and smooths again, re-choosing K and the smoothing parameters; the flags are recomputed on all observed weeks against the pass-2 fit (flag_2), so a week can be unflagged. If the set of weeks to exclude changes, a further pass is run with the new set, up to max_iter re-smoothings (pass max_iter + 1). When the set of flags of pass 1 is empty, pass 1 is final. flag holds the flags against the final fit (consistent with band_lo, band_hi) and excluded the weeks set to missing in the final fit; they coincide when the procedure converged (column converged of fits).

Flag types (per run of consecutive flagged weeks of flag): final when the run touches the last 4 weeks of the series; otherwise isolated when it is shorter than run_min weeks; otherwise level_shift when the median of the 8 unflagged observed weeks after the run minus the median of the 8 before it (on the seasonally adjusted scale, observed - seasonal) is at least the median band half-width over the run in absolute value, and interruption when it is smaller or cannot be computed (run at the start of the series).

Cost. Each pass chooses K with (max_harmonics + 1) * (n_backfit + 1) fits of the smooth Kalman model, then fits the method (n_backfit + 1 trend fits; gam_ar1: one bam per value of rho).

Examples

set.seed(1)
weeks <- data.table::as.IDate("2023-01-02") + 7L * (0:119)
tw <- as.numeric(weeks) / 7
mu <- 6 + 0.002 * seq_along(weeks) + 0.2 * sin(2 * pi * tw / (365.25 / 7))
n <- stats::rpois(120, exp(mu))
n[c(40, 80)] <- n[c(40, 80)] * 15
d <- data.table::data.table(source = "a", week = weeks, n = n)
rs <- robust_smooth(d, "source", "week", "n", method = "whittaker",
  harmonics = 1L)
rs[flag == TRUE, list(week, flag_type)]
#>          week flag_type
#>        <IDat>    <char>
#> 1: 2023-10-02  isolated
#> 2: 2024-07-08  isolated
attr(rs, "fits")
#>    source    method  pass     K    aicc_K parameter        value criterion
#>    <char>    <char> <int> <int>     <num>    <char>        <num>    <char>
#> 1:      a whittaker     1     1  112.4410    lambda 1.000000e+09       gcv
#> 2:      a whittaker     2     1 -384.6391    lambda 6.309573e+04       gcv
#>    criterion_value      edf   rho ic_ratio var_level var_slope var_obs   band
#>              <num>    <num> <num>    <num>     <num>     <num>   <num> <char>
#> 1:     0.119262266 2.000494    NA       NA        NA        NA      NA    mad
#> 2:     0.001646131 3.666668    NA       NA        NA        NA      NA    mad
#>    band_defined n_excluded n_flag iterations irls_converged q_select   phi
#>          <lgcl>      <int>  <int>      <int>         <lgcl>   <char> <num>
#> 1:         TRUE          0      2         NA             NA     <NA>    NA
#> 2:         TRUE          2      2         NA             NA     <NA>    NA
#>    loglik_profile q_at_edge phi_at_edge  final converged  error
#>             <num>    <lgcl>      <lgcl> <lgcl>    <lgcl> <char>
#> 1:             NA        NA          NA  FALSE      TRUE   <NA>
#> 2:             NA        NA          NA   TRUE      TRUE   <NA>
idx <- trend_index(rs, "source", "week",
  base_period = c("2023-01-02", "2023-12-31"), transform = "log")
